import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { resetAndSeed } from '../support/seed';

// Each charge line shows its quantity and unit, and the amount for that line (quantity times price).
test.describe('line item quantity and unit', () => {
  test('shows quantity, unit and per-line amount', { tag: '@core' }, async ({ page }) => {
    await resetAndSeed({
      clients: [{ id: 1, name: 'Acme Ltd', email: 'ops@acme.example' }],
      projects: [{ id: 1, name: 'Website Rebuild', clientId: 1 }],
      invoices: [{
        id: 1, projectId: 1, status: 'DRAFT',
        lineItems: [{ id: 1, description: 'Consulting', qty: 2, unit: 'hours', unitPrice: 50 }],
      }],
    });
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByTestId('nav-projects').click();
    await page.getByTestId('project-open-1').click();
    await page.getByTestId('invoice-open-1').click();

    const row = page.getByTestId('lineitem-row-1');
    await expect(row.getByTestId('lineitem-qty')).toHaveText('2');
    await expect(row.getByTestId('lineitem-unit')).toHaveText('hours');
    await expect(row.getByTestId('lineitem-amount')).toHaveText('$100.00');
  });
});

content.text:
Charge lines now have a unit as well as a quantity, and `bin/e2e` passes. Quantity and per-line amount were already on the invoice page, so the unit was the only missing piece.

One thing to know first: the task description calls the server "OfficeFloor", but it's actually a standard Spring Boot app (OfficeFloor only appears in the package name). I followed normal Spring conventions.

- **Database:** a new migration, `V23__line_item_unit.sql`, adds a `unit` column (up to 50 characters) to `invoice_line_item`. It's optional, because existing lines and invoices entered as a single amount don't have a unit.
- **Server:**
  - The line item entity, `Invoice`, `InvoiceService` and the line item request/response records all carry the unit.
  - A blank unit is saved as no unit, and units longer than 50 characters are rejected.
  - The `/__test__/seed` endpoint now accepts `unit` on line items.
- **Front end** (`invoice-detail.ts`):
  - The table has a new Unit column (`data-testid="lineitem-unit"`), next to the existing quantity (`lineitem-qty`) and amount (`lineitem-amount`, quantity × unit price). The Total row now spans one more column.
  - The "Add a line item" form has an optional Unit field (`lineitem-form-unit`), and editing a line in place has one too (`lineitem-edit-unit`).
  - No existing `data-testid` was renamed or removed.

The test only checks that a seeded unit is displayed. Saving a unit through the add and edit forms isn't covered by any test, and I haven't tried it in the running app.
